text:
I CAN NOW PROFILE THIS - the prepared data is in the repo - AND I CANNOT REPRODUCE ~9 s/node. I measure 0.4 s/node on the same data, the same mask, the same radius, the same conditions. This bead may be stale, and I would re-validate before optimizing anything.

SETUP, matching 05-crossnobis-uncertainty.R exactly: read_vol on data/subj1/mask4_vt.nii.gz, neuroim2_volume_domain, neuroim2_searchlights at RADIUS_MM = 11.25, CONDITIONS from models.R, lm_relation_fit over prep$response_runs with sampling_unit = "scan", cross_partitions, noise_precision(diag(577)) fixed-identity metric, plan_geometry.

  features 577   centres 577   mean support 44.8   q = 8

That is the exemplar's configuration, not a synthetic approximation.

MEASURED, JIT warmed, median of repeated calls:

  rdm_sampling_covariance(fixed_plan, fit, target = "plugin")      0.314 - 0.414 s
  sampling_covariance() x2 including the transport query           0.141 s
  FULL LOOP BODY as the exemplar writes it                         0.455 s/node

The README states ~9 s/node and derives 22 minutes for 120 nodes and 90 minutes for all 577 from it. At 0.455 s/node the full 577-centre sweep is about 4.4 minutes.

THE LEARNED-METRIC ARM IS NOT THE EXPLANATION. I suspected the heavier second arm was being timed. It is not: rdm_sampling_covariance on a crossnobis plan is REFUSED outright, and correctly -

  "Analytic RDM sampling covariance is unavailable because this plan's neural metric was
   learned. Version 0.1 does not propagate metric-estimation uncertainty; use a geometry plan
   with one common fixed metric or retain this result as a signed point estimate."

plan_crossnobis() itself builds in 1.233 s, once, not per node.

WHAT THE PROFILE SHOWS, on the second call with the JIT already warmed once:

  cmpfun / compiler:::tryCmpfun / genCode / cmp / cmpCall / tryInline    ~50 percent of total
  relation_fit_capabilities and .require_relation_fit_capability          22 percent
  grepl                                                                  13.9 percent self time

Half the remaining time is still the R byte-code compiler, which is warm-up rather than steady-state work, and a further fifth is capability validation. Neither is the covariance mathematics.

WHAT I AM AND AM NOT CLAIMING. I am not saying the original measurement was wrong. I am saying it does not reproduce on this machine against the current tree, and the gap is twenty-fold, which is far too large to be machine variation. The plausible explanations are that the figure predates a change that landed since, or that the original run measured under conditions I have not reconstructed - a cold session, a different tree, or the whole script including setup rather than the loop body.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP, before any optimization work: re-run 05 as written and check whether node_seconds still averages ~9 s. The script already instruments per-node time and RSS, so this is one run and no new code. If it now reports ~0.5 s/node, this bead is resolved and the README's Cost section needs updating rather than the function needing a precompute-once object.

If it DOES still report ~9 s/node while my direct reconstruction reports 0.455 s, then the cost is in something the script does that I did not reproduce, and diffing my script against 05 would localize it immediately. Either way that run is cheaper than optimizing.

One verified-good worth recording separately: the refusal quoted above is exactly what the exemplar header claims the arm is for - "the package declines to calibrate what it cannot calibrate, instead of returning a plausible number". It does, and the message names the reason, the version limit, and two alternatives.
